question.text: Chapter 9 says a PE fund 'invests primarily in equity or equity linked instruments or partnership interests of investee companies'. Which of the following is NOT included under 'equity-linked instruments' per the footnote in the chapter?

explanation.text: The Logic: The Chapter 9 footnote defines equity-linked instruments to include instruments convertible into equity shares, share warrants, preference shares, and debentures that are compulsorily or optionally convertible into equity. A senior secured non-convertible debenture is pure debt with no equity-conversion feature, so it falls outside that definition. The Trap: Options A, B and C each map directly to items expressly listed in the footnote (convertible instruments, share warrants, and convertible debentures). Option D is the distractor because PE funds do sometimes hold NCDs in hybrid sleeves, but a plain NCD is not "equity-linked" under the footnote. Note: The classification matters only as a matter of the definition in the footnote. The workbook does not prescribe specific category-drift or PPM-compliance steps in this passage, so reasoning should stay tied to the definition.
